## Orchestration plan — replay-an-enrichment-from-the-historical-trigger

**Flow:** A — one shared worktree, one combined diff, one commit + one PR.
**Tracker:** `github Launchmetrics/PLS-databricks#331` (this issue is the run's record).
**Tickets in → items out: 1 → 1.** Excluded issues: none. This parent is the `spec` issue — it is the run's record and the worker's spec context, not an item.

### Item

| | |
|---|---|
| **id** | `#332` |
| **title** | Replay an enrichment from the historical trigger |
| **ticket** | `#332` |
| **blockedBy** | none |
| **risk** | high — real state and contract surface (PENDING queueing, change-feed checkpoint, recovery markers) |

**File scope**

```
projects/enrichments/prometheus_generic_trigger/
  tasks/prometheus_historical_trigger.py          # cli() + run(), replay path
  resources/prometheus_generic_trigger_jobs.yml   # run-now param, empty by default
  tests/unit/test_prometheus_historical_trigger.py
  tests/integration/test_historical_trigger.py
  utils/contract_reader.py                        # only if reuse falls short
```

### Graph

None. Native `blockedBy` is empty and #332's `## Blocked by` says "None (can start immediately)" — the two sources agree.

### Waves

- **wave 1:** `#332`

### Per-item notes

- **High risk** — full adversarial review (every acceptance criterion verified in code), not a mechanical pass.
- The job definition must carry the replay parameter **empty**; a defaulted value would turn the nightly run into a replay.
- `utils/contract_reader.py` is in scope only as a fallback — `read_all_valid()` already reads enabled contracts *including ended ones*, which is exactly the replay's read, so reuse is preferred over a new method.
- No reset, no push, no force-push. No acceptance criterion reaches outside this repo.

### Models

Role defaults, **no override** — worker + ponytail `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, code-review `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.

### End of run

Combined-diff ponytail pass → commit + one PR (human approval gate) → `gh` comment on `#332`, no close, no label change.

## Run summary — replay an enrichment from the historical trigger

Orchestrated run for this spec: one item, flow A (single shared PR). Manager thread `thr_hfd8bzq2iy`.

| Item | Outcome | Worker | Review | Ponytail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #332 | done | `thr_szuc8vevh9` | clean on round 2 (`thr_zvgbvb64q` findings → fixed → `thr_rx3ggmuz3i` clean) | `thr_gn8sp77qpv`, findings adjudicated (see below) |

**What shipped** (uncommitted until the PR gate): `--replay_enrichment` on the existing historical trigger, empty by default. A non-empty value takes a stateless replay path that reads the enrichment's enabled contracts (including ended, excluding disabled) via `ContractReader.read_all_valid()`, queues every in-scope document including already-populated ones, carries already-enriched out-of-scope brands in the payload, and never reads or saves the change-feed checkpoint, never consults or writes the PROCESSED marker, and never emits recovery. Unknown enrichment name fails the run; a registered enrichment with no enabled contracts queues nothing and succeeds. The saved job definition passes the parameter empty, so the nightly path is unchanged.

**Verification**: `lm-pyconv check` exit 0; `pytest prometheus_generic_trigger/tests/` 219 passed, including the pre-existing nightly-path regression tests.

**Ponytail pass findings, not applied in-run** (out of the pass's remit because the spec explicitly requests this coverage): the pass proposed deleting five replay unit tests that repeat scenarios also covered in the new integration tests. #331 *Testing Decisions* designates the unit seam with a mocked contract reader and mocked consolidation area as the coverage seam and lists those scenarios to cover, so the deletion is a spec-author call; a follow-up is recorded on the run. Two cosmetic notes (the `_initialize_enrichment` docstring no longer describes both modes, and one job comment says "every in-scope document" where print-skip and prerequisite gating still trim it) are recorded as follow-ups as well.

**PR**: opened at the end of the run; this comment is not edited afterwards — the closing lines live in the PR body.

From v1->v3 and from v1-> v4.

(it's true that we could do the other way around just while we are deploying the new version if we want to do one step at a time)

The event_percolation is the other way around because we introduced a newer version but we are still consolidating with the old one.

At first glance it confused me with the `pass_through` enrichment name. AI suggested me `_identity` but we have the same problem :) and also `_noop`/`_no-op` that maybe did not collision with anything.
yes, is to force to have all enrichments here to not miss anything by mistake

**[NIT]** **confidence 55%** - docstring doesn't mention the new `replay` behavior

---

**Why:** The docstring still describes only the nightly semantics ("insert any not-yet-enriched ones", always emit PROCESSED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED), but `replay=True` ignores done-state entirely and skips marker emission altogether. A future reader relying on the docstring could miss this significant behavior fork.

---

**Fix:** Add a line to the docstring noting that `replay=True` bypasses the done-state filter and returns before any marker is written.
